The '''2020–21 season''' was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s 107th competitive season, 32nd consecutive season in the top flight of English football, 29th consecutive season in the [[Premier League]], and 115th year in existence as a football club.<ref>{{Cite web|title=History|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/about-chelsea/history|website=chelseafc.com|date=1 July 2020}}</ref> The season covered the period from 1 July 2020 to 30 June 2021.

Prior to the 2020–21 season, Chelsea made numerous high-profile signings in the transfer market, bringing in the likes of [[Timo Werner]], [[Kai Havertz]], [[Ben Chilwell]], [[Hakim Ziyech]], and [[Thiago Silva]] in the close-season, as well as [[Édouard Mendy]] shortly after the season began. The Blues began this season under the management of former Chelsea player [[Frank Lampard]], in his second season at the club. However, Lampard was sacked in January and replaced by German manager [[Thomas Tuchel]], who guided the club to European glory, as on 29 May, Chelsea defeated fellow English side [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]], their second title in the competition, and their first since [[2012 UEFA Champions League final|2012]].

The season was the first since [[2012–13 Chelsea F.C. season|2012–13]] without [[Willian (footballer, born 1988)|Willian]], who departed to [[Arsenal F.C|Arsenal]].

=== September ===

Chelsea played their first game of the new [[2020–21 Premier League|Premier League]] season on 14 September 2020, travelling to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] and earning a 3–1 away victory, courtesy of goals from [[Jorginho (footballer, born December 1991)|Jorginho]], [[Kurt Zouma]] and [[Reece James (footballer, born 1999)|Reece James]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Brighton 1-3 Chelsea: Frank Lampard wants title challenge after starting season with win |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54052535 |website=BBC Sport |date=14 September 2020}}</ref> On 20 September, Chelsea welcomed defending champions [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]]. [[Andreas Christensen]] was [[Dismissal (football)|dismissed]] in the first half after a naive challenge on [[Sadio Mané]], who then proceeded to score [[Brace (association football)|two goals]] inside four minutes for Liverpool, with goalkeeper [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] making a crucial mistake for Mané's second goal. New signing [[Timo Werner]] managed to win a penalty for Chelsea, but Jorginho had his effort saved by [[Alisson Becker|Alisson]], his first penalty miss in nine attempts, as the match ended in a 2–0 defeat for Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0-2 Liverpool: Sadio Mane nets double against 10-man Blues |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54135434 |website=BBC Sport |date=20 September 2020}}</ref>

Three days later, Chelsea faced [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] in the [[EFL Cup]], which ended in a 6–0 win for Chelsea, with [[Kai Havertz]] scoring a [[Hat-trick#Association football|hat-trick]] for the Blues.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 6-0 Barnsley: Kai Havertz hat-trick sends Blues through |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54190608 |website=BBC Sport |date=23 September 2020}}</ref> Chelsea then travelled to [[The Hawthorns]] to play [[West Bromwich Albion]]. Chelsea were 3–0 down at half-time, but goals from [[Mason Mount]], [[Callum Hudson-Odoi]], and [[Tammy Abraham]] in stoppage-time managed to seal a draw as the match ended 3–3.<ref>{{cite web |title=West Brom 3-3 Chelsea: Tammy Abraham scores stoppage-time equaliser |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54215342 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 September 2020}}</ref> On 29 September, Chelsea took on [[Chelsea F.C.–Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry|London rivals]] [[Tottenham Hotspur]] in the round of 16 in the EFL Cup. Timo Werner scored his first Chelsea goal to put the Blues ahead, but [[Erik Lamela]] managed to equalise in the second half. Chelsea would go on to lose 5–4 on penalties, with Mason Mount missing the decisive penalty and Chelsea finding themselves eliminated from the EFL Cup.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carabao Cup: Tottenham 1-1 Chelsea (5-4 pens) |url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54298219 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 September 2020}}</ref>

Reece James' goal against Brighton was nominated for the [[Premier League Goal of the Month]] award, but was won by [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]'s [[James Maddison]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Watch September 2020's Budweiser Goal of the Month contenders |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1848487 |website=Premier League |date=2 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Maddison wins September 2020's Budweiser Goal of the Month |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1857311 |website=Premier League |date=9 October 2020}}</ref>

=== October ===

Chelsea's first match of October was against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at home. After no goals in the first half, Chelsea managed to win 4–0, as [[Ben Chilwell]] registered a goal and an assist on his Premier League debut for Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 4-0 Crystal Palace: Ben Chilwell scores on first Premier League start since move|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54305844 |website=BBC Sport |date=3 October 2020}}</ref> Two weeks later, on 17 October, Chelsea welcomed [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] to Stamford Bridge. Timo Werner scored his first Premier League goals for Chelsea as the Blues were leading 2–0 inside 28 minutes, with [[Danny Ings]] managing to pull a goal back for the Saints before half-time. [[Che Adams]] scored an equaliser for Southampton 57 minutes in, but Chelsea instantly responded with a Kai Havertz goal two minutes later, his first in the Premier League. Chelsea were pegged back again in the 92nd minute, with [[Jannik Vestergaard]] levelling the game, as Chelsea managed to come out of the game with a frustrating 3–3 draw.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 3-3 Southampton: Blues must cut out individual errors — Lampard|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54489178 |website=BBC Sport |date=17 October 2020}}</ref> In their next two games, Chelsea drew back-to-back games 0–0, first against [[Sevilla F.C.|Sevilla]] at home in their first [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] game of the season, and then again away at [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the Premier League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0-0 Sevilla: Frank Lampard's side held in opening Champions League group game|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54559696 |website=BBC Sport |date=20 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Manchester United 0-0 Chelsea: Hosts still searching for first home win this season|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54580512 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2020}}</ref>

Chelsea then defeated [[FK Krasnodar|Krasnodar]] 4–0 away in the Champions League, with Callum Hudson-Odoi, Timo Werner, [[Hakim Ziyech]], and [[Christian Pulisic]] all on target for the Blues.<ref>{{cite web |title=FK Krasnodar 0-4 Chelsea: Hakim Ziyech and Christian Pulisic strikes put seal on emphatic win|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54713315 |website=BBC Sport |date=28 October 2020}}</ref> In Chelsea's final game of the month on 31 October, they defeated [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] 3–0 away, with Hakim Ziyech scoring and assisting on his first Premier League start, with additional goals from Kurt Zouma and Timo Werner sealing the win for Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web |title=Burnley 0-3 Chelsea: Hakim Ziyech grabs first league goal in Blues win|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54671336 |website=BBC Sport |date=31 October 2020}}</ref>

As a result of his performances throughout the month, [[Thiago Silva]] was nominated for the [[Premier League Player of the Month]] award, which was eventually won by Tottenham Hotspur's [[Son Heung-min|Heung-min Son]], and Timo Werner's first goal against Southampton was nominated for Premier League Goal of the Month, but was instead given to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]]'s [[Manuel Lanzini]].<ref>{{cite web |title=October 2020's EA Sports Player of the Month shortlist|url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1885087 |website=Premier League |date=7 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Son wins October 2020 EA Sports Player of the Month award|url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1894987 |website=Premier League |date=13 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=October 2020's Budweiser Goal of the Month contenders|url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1885097 |website=Premier League |date=7 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Lanzini claims October 2020's Budweiser Goal of the Month award|url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1894985 |website=Premier League |date=13 November 2020}}</ref>

=== November ===

Chelsea begun November with a 3–0 home victory over [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] in the Champions League, with the goals coming from two Timo Werner penalties and a Tammy Abraham strike.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 3-0 Rennes: Timo Werner scores twice from the penalty spot |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54799447 |website=BBC Sport |date=4 November 2020}}</ref> Three days later, in Chelsea's last match before the November international break, Chelsea faced bottom of the league [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] at home, who had lost seven out of their first eight Premier League games this season. The match ended in a comfortable 4–1 win for the Blues, which saw Hakim Ziyech pick up two assists.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 4-1 Sheffield United: Comfortable win for Blues leaves Sheff Utd bottom |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54758066 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 November 2020}}</ref>

After the international break, Chelsea returned on 21 November to face [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[St James' Park]]. Chelsea ran out 2–0 winners, with a [[Federico Fernández (footballer)|Federico Fernández]] [[own goal]] and a goal from Tammy Abraham sealing the win for Chelsea, marking the first time Chelsea were top of the Premier League under [[Frank Lampard]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Newcastle United 0-2 Chelsea: Frank Lampard's Blues make it five wins out of five |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54941197 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 November 2020}}</ref> Chelsea won their sixth consecutive game in a row in their next match against Rennes in the Champions League, which saw Callum Hudson-Odoi and [[Olivier Giroud]] on the scoresheet in a 2–1 away victory, sealing qualification for the Champions League round of 16.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rennes 1-2 Chelsea: Blues seal early qualification to Champions League last 16|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55047362 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 November 2020}}</ref> Chelsea next had inform London rivals Tottenham Hotspur to play at Stamford Bridge, who had already eliminated Chelsea from the EFL Cup back in September. The match ended in goalless 0–0 draw, which saw Tottenham ascend to the top of the league.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0-0 Tottenham Hotspur: Spurs return to the top of the Premier League|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55032761 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 November 2020}}</ref>

Ben Chilwell's performances throughout November earned a nomination for the Premier League Player of the Month award, which was by Manchester United's [[Bruno Fernandes]], and Frank Lampard's managerial duties saw him nominated for [[Premier League Manager of the Month]], which was instead by Tottenham Hotspur's [[José Mourinho]].<ref>{{cite web |title=November 2020's EA Sports Player of the Month nominees |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1919105 |website=Premier League |date=5 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Fernandes wins November 2020's EA Sports Player of the Month |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1931610 |website=Premier League |date=11 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=November 2020 Barclays Manager of the Month shortlist |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1919089 |website=Premier League |date=5 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mourinho named November 2020 Barclays Manager of the Month |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/1931855 |website=Premier League |date=11 December 2020}}</ref>

=== December ===

Chelsea's first game of the busy December period was at Sevilla in the Champions League group stage. Frank Lampard's Blues ran out 4–0 winners, with Olivier Giroud scoring all four goals for Chelsea, ensuring that the Blues' top spot in their group was secured.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sevilla 0-4 Chelsea: Olivier Giroud scores four to put Blues top of group|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55135784 |website=BBC Sport |date=2 December 2020}}</ref> On December 5, they welcomed [[Chelsea F.C.–Leeds United F.C. rivalry|bitter rivals]] [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] to Stamford Bridge, in Chelsea's first home game with 2,000 fans in attendance. Leeds took a shock lead just five minutes through [[Patrick Bamford]], but the Blues managed to equalise with an Olivier Giroud goal and defeated their rivals 3–1 to go top of the Premier League, with Kurt Zouma and Christian Pulisic also adding to the goals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 3-1 Leeds United: Blues go top after comeback win in front of fans|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55111848 |website=BBC Sport |date=5 December 2020}}</ref> Chelsea played out a 1–1 home draw three days later against Krasnodar, in their final group stage game of the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 1-1 Krasnodar: Jorginho penalty earns Blues point|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55219536 |website=BBC Sport |date=8 December 2020}}</ref>

Next, Chelsea travelled to [[Goodison Park]] to play [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 12 December. The match ended in a 1–0 loss for Chelsea, their first away defeat of the season, putting an end to their 17-game unbeaten run and losing ground in the title race, with Tottenham and Liverpool both ahead of Chelsea, and with a game in hand.<ref>{{cite web |title=Everton 1-0 Chelsea: Gylfi Sigurdsson penalty gives hosts Goodison Park win |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55197156 |website=BBC Sport |date=12 December 2020}}</ref> Chelsea then followed this up by losing again away to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]], with a 95th-minute winner from [[Pedro Neto]] sealing a 2–1 win for Wolves.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wolverhampton Wanderers 2-1 Chelsea: Pedro Neto scores late winner for Wolves |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55225714 |website=BBC Sport |date=15 December 2020}}</ref> Chelsea returned to winning ways in a 3–0 home victory against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], with a header from Thiago Silva and a [[Brace (association football)|brace]] from Tammy Abraham sealing an emphatic victory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 3-0 West Ham: Tammy Abraham scores twice in Blues win |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55297949 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 December 2020}}</ref>

On 26 December, Chelsea travelled to [[North London]] to play out-of-form [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at the [[Emirates Stadium]]; Arsenal  were in 15th place and were winless in the last seven matches entering this game. The Gunners took a shock 2–0 lead at half-time, courtesy of an [[Alexandre Lacazette]] penalty and a [[Granit Xhaka]] free kick, before [[Bukayo Saka]] added to Arsenal's shock lead in the 56th minute. Tammy Abraham scored a consolation goal in the 85th minute, and Jorginho had a penalty saved in added time by [[Bernd Leno]], to ensure no comeback was to happen for the Blues, in a humiliating 3–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal 3-1 Chelsea: Gunners end winless run in Premier League |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55373755 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2020}}</ref> Chelsea closed out 2020 with a 1–1 home draw against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], with Olivier Giroud and [[Anwar El Ghazi]] scoring the only goals of the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 1-1 Aston Villa: Anwar El Ghazi earns point for visitors |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55391050 |website=BBC Sport |date=28 December 2020}}</ref>

=== January ===

Chelsea's first match of 2021 was at home against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] on 3 January. Chelsea struggled greatly throughout the game and were 3–0 down inside 34 minutes, with the goals coming from [[İlkay Gündoğan]], [[Phil Foden]], and former Chelsea man [[Kevin De Bruyne]]. Callum Hudson-Odoi scored a consolation goal in the 92nd minute, as the Blues suffered another embarrassing 3–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 1-3 Manchester City: Visitors up to fifth in ruthless display |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55456856 |website=BBC Sport |date=3 January 2021}}</ref> The next week, Chelsea begun their quest for the [[2020–21 FA Cup|FA Cup]] after [[2020 FA Cup Final|coming up short the previous year]], starting off their journey with a comfortable 4–0 home victory against [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] in the third round, with Mason Mount, Timo Werner, Callum Hudson-Odoi, and Kai Havertz finding the net for Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 4-0 Morecambe: Timo Werner scores in FA Cup win |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55575484 |website=BBC Sport |date=10 January 2021}}</ref>

Chelsea then made a trip to [[Craven Cottage]] to take on [[West London derby|West London rivals]] [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]]. The game saw Fulham fullback [[Antonee Robinson]] being shown a red card after a dangerous challenge on [[César Azpilicueta]]. Mason Mount managed to score the only goal of the match in the 78th minute, as Chelsea earned a hard-fought 1–0 win against their rivals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fulham 0-1 Chelsea: Mason Mount goal settles London derby |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55583120 |website=BBC Sport |date=16 January 2021}}</ref> Chelsea's next match was away at high-flying [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], who at this point were second in the league. Chelsea went on to lose this match 2–0, with first-half goals from [[Wilfred Ndidi]] and [[James Maddison]] piling more misery on the Blues' bad run of form.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leicester City 2-0 Chelsea: Leicester win to go top of Premier League |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55627849 |website=BBC Sport |date=19 January 2021}}</ref> Frank Lampard's final game took place on 24 January, as Chelsea defeated [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] 3–1 in the FA Cup. However, this wasn't enough to save Lampard's job, as the very next day, Chelsea announced the sacking of Lampard after their poor run of form that included only two wins from their past eight league matches.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 3-1 Luton: Tammy Abraham hat-trick in FA Cup |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55770051 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 January 2021}}</ref>

The following day, it was announced that former [[Borussia Dortmund]] and [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] manager [[Thomas Tuchel]] would be replacing Lampard as the manager of Chelsea.<ref name="ESPNTuchel">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/chelsea/story/4298088/chelsea-appoint-tuchel-to-replace-lampard-as-manager|title=Chelsea appoint Tuchel to replace Lampard as manager|website=ESPN|date=26 January 2021|access-date=27 January 2021}}</ref> Tuchel's first match in charge took place two days later, with Chelsea taking on [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] at Stamford Bridge. The match ended in a frustrating 0–0 stalemate, with Chelsea having 79% possession of the ball but were unable to find the net. Tuchel stated after the match that "we will build a team nobody wants to play against".<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0-0 Wolverhampton Wanderers: Thomas Tuchel suffers frustrating start |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55728235 |website=BBC Sport |date=27 January 2021}}</ref> Chelsea's final match of the month was against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] at home, which saw Tuchel claim his first win as Chelsea manager, as goals from César Azpilicueta and [[Marcos Alonso (footballer, born 1990)|Marcos Alonso]] sealed a 2–0 victory for the Blues.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2-0 Burnley: Thomas Tuchel records first win as boss |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55769201 |website=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2021}}</ref> Alonso's strike against the Clarets earned him a nomination for the Premier League Goal of the Month award, eventually won by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s [[Mohamed Salah]].<ref>{{cite web |title= January 2021's Budweiser Goal of the Month contenders |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/2008340 |website=Premier League |date=5 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title= Salah wins January 2021 Budweiser Goal of the Month |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/2021392 |website=Premier League |date=12 February 2021}}</ref>

=== February ===

Chelsea opened February with three consecutive away victories at [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] in the league, and [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] in the FA Cup.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tottenham 0-1 Chelsea: Jorginho condemns Spurs to third Premier League loss in a row |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55836547 |website=BBC Sport |date=4 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sheffield United 1-2 Chelsea: Visitors maintain unbeaten start to Tuchel reign |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55875681 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Barnsley 0-1 Chelsea: Tammy Abraham scores winner at Oakwell |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55955768 |website=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2021}}</ref> On 15 February, Chelsea welcomed [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] to Stamford Bridge, with Chelsea winning 2–0 to claim their fifth victory in a row in all competitions, as Timo Werner ended his 14-game goal drought in the Premier League, dating back to November.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2-0 Newcastle: Timo Werner ends goal drought in Blues win |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55975612 |website=BBC Sport |date=15 February 2021}}</ref>

Chelsea then took the trip to [[St Mary's Stadium]] to take on [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] on 20 February, who had lost their last six Premier League matches in a row, including a [[Manchester United F.C. 9–0 Southampton F.C.|9–0]] defeat at [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. The Blues could only manage a 1–1 draw, with [[Takumi Minamino]] opening the scoring in the first half before Mason Mount equalised with a penalty in the second half.<ref>{{cite web |title=Southampton 1-1 Chelsea: Ralph Hassenhutl hopes Saints will kick on draw |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56033661 |website=BBC Sport |date=20 February 2021}}</ref> Three days later, Chelsea travelled to Spain to play [[Atlético Madrid]] in the first leg of their Champions League [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|round of 16]] tie. Chelsea won the match 1–0, with an Olivier Giroud bicycle kick sealing the first leg win and a crucial away goal for Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web |title=Atletico Madrid 0-1 Chelsea: Olivier Giroud scores winner in Champions League last 16 first leg |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56159008 |website=BBC Sport |date=23 February 2021}}</ref> Chelsea returned to Premier League action on 28 February, playing out a dull goalless stalemate against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at Stamford Bridge.<ref>{{cite web |title=Premier League: Chelsea 0-0 Manchester United – More VAR controversy in stalemate |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56143444 |website=BBC Sport |date=28 February 2021}}</ref>

Chelsea's league performances under Thomas Tuchel in February earned the German a nomination for the Premier League Manager of the Month award, which was won by [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s [[Pep Guardiola]].<ref>{{cite web |title=February 2021's Barclays Manager of the Month shortlist |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/2050751 |website=Premier League |date=8 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Guardiola earns Man City double with February 2021 Barclays Manager award |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/2061416 |website=Premier League |date=12 March 2021}}</ref>

=== March ===

Chelsea's first match of the month saw them take on [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]], who had lost their last four home games after going on a 68-game home unbeaten run between April 2017 and January 2021, the second-longest in league history, with the record belonging to Chelsea themselves after going unbeaten at home for 86 games between March 2004 and October 2008. Chelsea defeated the Reds 1–0, with a superb Mason Mount strike in the 42nd minute condemning Liverpool to their fifth home loss in a row, and Tuchel extending his unbeaten run to 10 games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Liverpool 0-1 Chelsea: Reds 'cannot rely on the past' – Andy Robertson |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56191315 |website=BBC Sport |date=4 March 2021}}</ref> Next, Chelsea defeated [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] 2–0, with an own goal form [[Ben Godfrey]] and a Jorginho penalty sealing the victory for the Blues.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2-0 Everton: Thomas Tuchel praises Kai Havertz as Blues strengthen top-four hopes |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56234678 |website=BBC Sport |date=8 March 2021}}</ref>

The Blues then travelled to [[Elland Road]] to play bitter rivals [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 13 March, which ended in a 0–0 draw.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leeds United 0-0 Chelsea: Thomas Tuchel's unbeaten run stretches to 12 games |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56247499 |website=BBC Sport |date=13 March 2021}}</ref> Chelsea then played the second leg of their Champions League round of 16 tie against [[Atlético Madrid]], this time at home, with the Blues heading into the game with a 1–0 advantage and an away goal. Chelsea earned a 2–0 victory, with goals from Hakim Ziyech and [[Emerson Palmieri]] ensuring Chelsea's progression to the quarter finals of the Champions League, the first time they had done so since the [[2013–14 Chelsea F.C. season|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2-0 Atletico Madrid (3-0 agg): Hosts reach Champions League last eight |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56419713 |website=BBC Sport |date=17 March 2021}}</ref> The victory also meant that Tuchel became the first Chelsea manager to go unbeaten in his first 13 matches in charge of the club, surpassing the previous record of 12 held by [[Luiz Felipe Scolari]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.90min.com/in/posts/12-games-unbeaten-thomas-tuchel-matches-luiz-felipe-scolari-and-jose-mourinho-s-chelsea-record-01f0qxbnbegh|title=12 Games Unbeaten: Thomas Tuchel Matches Luiz Felipe Scolari and Jose Mourinho's Chelsea Record|website=90 Min|date=14 March 2021|access-date=17 March 2021}}</ref> Chelsea followed this up by defeating [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] in the quarter finals of the FA Cup, sending the Blues through to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2-0 Sheffield United: Blues into FA Cup semi-finals after win at Stamford Bridge |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56415023 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 March 2021}}</ref> Chelsea then went on a brief hiatus for the March international break.

Chelsea were nominated for all three Premier League awards in March, with Andreas Christensen's defensive performances earning him a nomination for the Premier League Player of the Month award, and Mason Mount's goal against Liverpool also being nominated for Premier League Goal of the Month.<ref>{{cite web |title=March 2021's EA Sports Player of the Month contenders |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/2075910 |website=Premier League |date=29 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Budweiser Goal of the Month shortlist for March 2021 |url= https://www.premierleague.com/news/2075913 |website=Premier League |date=29 March 2021}}</ref> Thomas Tuchel was nominated for the Premier League Manager of the Month award for the second consecutive month, this time being honoured with the award.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2080145|title=Tuchel claims Barclays Manager of the Month award |website=Premier League |date=2 April 2021 |access-date=2 April 2021}}</ref>

=== April ===

Chelsea's first match after the international break saw them welcome relegation-fighting [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] to Stamford Bridge. Christian Pulisic gave Chelsea the lead 27 minutes in but just two minutes later, Thiago Silva was sent off after receiving a second yellow card. The Blues found themselves 2–1 down at half-time via a stoppage-time brace from [[Matheus Pereira (footballer, born 1996)|Matheus Pereira]]. Goals from [[Callum Robinson]] and [[Mbaye Diagne (footballer)|Mbaye Diagne]] gave the Baggies a shocking 4–1 lead. Mason Mount managed to pull one back for Chelsea, but another goal from Callum Robinson in added time capped off an embarrassing 2–5 defeat for Chelsea, ending Thomas Tuchel's 14-game unbeaten streak as manager. It was the first time Chelsea had conceded 5 goals at home since a 3–5 defeat against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in [[2011–12 Chelsea F.C. season|2011]], and was also the first time they had lost to West Bromwich Albion at Stamford Bridge since 1978.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2021/apr/03/chelsea-v-west-brom-premier-league-live|last=Glendenning|first=Barry|title=Chelsea 2-5 West Brom: Premier League – as it happened|work=The Guardian|date=3 April 2021|access-date=3 April 2021}}</ref> Chelsea bounced back from the humiliation in their next game, which was the first leg of their Champions League quarter final tie against [[FC Porto|Porto]] away, which saw a fine Mason Mount strike and a late Ben Chilwell goal give Chelsea a 2–0 victory with two crucial away goals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Porto 0-2 Chelsea: Mason Mount scores his first Champions League goal |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56653905 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 April 2021}}</ref>

Chelsea then travelled to [[South London]] to take on [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] away on 10 April. Goals from Kai Havertz, Kurt Zouma and a brace from Christian Pulisic saw Chelsea run out 4–1 winners, the first time they had scored more than two goals under Tuchel.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crystal Palace 1-4 Chelsea: Tuchel demands more from Havertz as Blues return to top four |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56622156 |website=BBC Sport |date=10 April 2021}}</ref> The Blues then played Porto in the second leg of the Champions League quarter finals, heading into the game with a 2–0 advantage and two away goals. Chelsea were defeated 1–0 thanks to a late [[Mehdi Taremi]] overhead kick, but did enough to make it through to the Champions League semi-finals, winning 2–1 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web |title=Champions League quarter-finals: Chelsea 0-1 Porto |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56721849 |website=BBC Sport |date=13 April 2021}}</ref> Four days later, Chelsea defeated [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the FA Cup semi-finals, with Hakim Ziyech scoring the winner to help Chelsea advance to the [[2021 FA Cup Final|FA Cup Final]] for the second consecutive year.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Murray|first=Scott|date=17 April 2021|title=Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City: FA Cup semi-final – as it happened|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2021/apr/17/chelsea-v-manchester-city-fa-cup-semi-final-live|access-date=17 April 2021}}</ref>

On 18 April, it was announced that Chelsea would be a founding member of the newly formed [[European Super League]], a proposed annual club football competition to be contested by twenty of Europe's most elite football clubs.<ref name="announcement">{{Cite press release |title=Leading European football clubs announce new Super League competition |date=18 April 2021 |url=https://thesuperleague.com/press.html|access-date=18 April 2021 |work=The Super League}}</ref> On 20 April, after two days of widespread backlash from the United Kingdom government including Prime Minister [[Boris Johnson]], [[FIFA]], [[UEFA]], the [[The Football Association|FA]], other Premier League clubs, supporters, players, and broadcasters, and after Chairman [[Bruce Buck]] met with players, Chelsea announced their intention to withdraw from the competition.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chelsea to withdraw from European Super League|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4216756/2021/04/20/chelsea-to-withdraw-from-european-super-league/|website=theathletic.com|date=21 April 2021|access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref>  This led to the five other English clubs all pulling out later that night.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56823501#:~:text=Manchester%20City%20were%20the%20first,have%20all%20now%20followed%20suit.|title=European Super League: All six Premier League teams withdraw from competition|website=BBC|date=21 April 2021|access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref> By 21 April, the Super League announced it was suspending its operations.<ref>{{Cite web|date=21 April 2021|title=Super League suspended: Why English clubs pulled out, and what's next for them and UEFA|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/blog-marcottis-musings/story/4365465/super-league-suspended-why-english-clubs-pulled-outwhats-next-for-them-and-uefa|access-date=21 April 2021|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 20 April, Chelsea played out a 0–0 home draw against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], losing some ground in the top four race.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0-0 Brighton & Hove Albion: Hosts held on dramatic night for European football |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56728001 |website=BBC Sport |date=20 April 2021}}</ref> Four days later, the Blues defeated [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] 1–0 away, with a Timo Werner goal sealing the win for Chelsea. Chelsea's final match of April was against [[Real Madrid F.C.|Real Madrid]] away in the first leg of the Champions League semi-finals. Chelsea took the lead through Christian Pulisic, but [[Karim Benzema]] equalised for Real Madrid later in the first half, as the match ended in a 1–1 draw, with Chelsea entering the second leg at home a crucial away goal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Karim Benzema earns Real Madrid draw against Chelsea |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56880436 |website=BBC Sport |date=27 April 2021}}</ref>

=== May ===

Chelsea's first fixture of May saw them defeat West London rivals [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] 2–0, thanks to a brace from Kai Havertz.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2-0 Fulham: Kai Havertz double sends Cottagers closer to drop |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56869465 |website=BBC Sport |date=1 May 2021}}</ref> On 5 May, Chelsea welcomed [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] to Stamford Bridge for the second leg of their semi-final, with the score being level at 1–1 and Chelsea heading into the match with an away goal. Timo Werner gave Chelsea the lead in the 28th minute, before a late tap-in from Mason Mount booked Chelsea their place in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League Final]] in [[Istanbul]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0269-1234c3a15e7c-42c644e8c262-1000--chelsea-2-0-real-madrid-hosts-cruise-into-third-final/|title=Chelsea 2-0 Real Madrid: Hosts cruise into third final|website=UEFA|date=5 May 2021}}</ref> Their win set up an all-English affair after [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] had secured their maiden appearance in the final the day before, defeating [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] over two legs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/05/chelsea-real-madrid-champions-league-semi-final-second-leg-match-report|title=Chelsea power past Real Madrid to set up all-English Champions League final|website=The Guardian|date=5 May 2021}}</ref>

Chelsea's next match in the Premier League was against their Champions League final opponents, Manchester City, at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]]. [[Raheem Sterling]] scored first for the Citizens 44 minutes in, with [[Sergio Agüero]] having a penalty saved by [[Édouard Mendy]] just before half-time. Hakim Ziyech scored the equaliser for the Blues in the 63rd minute, before a stoppage-time goal from Marcos Alonso saw Chelsea run out 2–1 winners, as Thomas Tuchel made it two consecutive victories against [[Pep Guardiola]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Manchester City 1-2 Chelsea: Aguero misses penalty as Chelsea make City wait for Premier League title |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56953530 |website=BBC Sport |date=8 May 2021}}</ref> Next, Chelsea took on ninth-placed [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at home, with [[Mikel Arteta]]'s Gunners already enduring a [[2020–21 Arsenal F.C. season|poor season]]. Chelsea were shockingly defeated 1–0, with a poor back pass from Jorginho allowing [[Emile Smith Rowe]] to score the winner for Arsenal, with Christian Pulisic also having a goal disallowed by [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] due to a handball. This was the first time had Chelsea had lost to Arsenal at home in nearly a decade, since a 3–5 defeat in October 2011.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0-1 Arsenal: Blues boss Thomas Tuchel accepts responsibility for loss|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56990160 |website=BBC Sport |date=12 May 2021}}</ref>

On 15 May, Chelsea faced [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] in the [[2021 FA Cup final|FA Cup Final]], which was Chelsea's first chance of winning silverware this season. It was a frustrating game for Tuchel's Blues, as they were denied by [[Kasper Schmeichel]] multiple times throughout the game, with a [[Youri Tielemans]] stunner in the 63rd minute putting Leicester 1–0 up. Chelsea thought they had found their equaliser through Ben Chilwell in the 88th minute, but was ruled out by VAR for offside, as the Foxes won their first ever FA Cup and Chelsea had lost the FA Cup Final for the second straight year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 0-1 Leicester City: Foxes list FA Cup for first time after Youri Tielemans stunner |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57055571 |website=BBC Sport |date=15 May 2021}}</ref> Chelsea had an immediate rematch against Leicester City three days later in the Premier League, with goals from [[Antonio Rüdiger]] and Jorginho giving Chelsea a 2–1 victory and strengthening their top four hopes, while leaving Leicester's Champions League hopes in danger.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chelsea 2-1 Leicester City: Blues beat Foxes in crucial top-four showdown |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57066729 |website=BBC Sport |date=18 May 2021}}</ref> Chelsea's final Premier League match of the season saw them travel to [[Birmingham]] to face [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], on 23 May. Chelsea would go on to lose 2–1, but still finished fourth and secured their place in [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|next season's Champions League]], as elsewhere, Leicester City lost to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/23/aston-villa-chelsea-premier-league-match-report|title=Chelsea qualify for Champions League despite stumbling at Aston Villa|website=The Guardian|date=23 May 2021|access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref>

On 29 May, Chelsea faced [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League Final]]. It was the third time in Chelsea's 116-year history that they had competed in the [[Champions League final]], losing against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in [[2008 UEFA Champions League final|2008]] and defeating [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in [[2012 UEFA Champions League final|2012]]. Chelsea went into the match as the underdogs, similarly to 2012, and defeated Manchester City 1–0 to win the Champions League, with Kai Havertz's goal in the first-half goal sealing Chelsea's second Champions League title. Chelsea became the third English club to win the Champions League multiple times, after [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] ([[2005 UEFA Champions League final|2005]], [[2019 UEFA Champions League final|2019]]) and Manchester United ([[1999 UEFA Champions League final|1999]], [[2008 UEFA Champions League final|2008]]).<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0269-12650cedca55-37515f69768e-1000/ |title=Man. City 0–1 Chelsea: Havertz gives Blues second Champions League triumph |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=29 May 2021 |access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2020–21 FA Cup}}

Chelsea got the right to enter the [[2020–21 FA Cup]] in the third round proper along with the other Premier League and Championship clubs. The third round draw was made on 30 November, and Chelsea were drawn against [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier League and Championship clubs join Emirates FA Cup After third round Draw |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2020/nov/30/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-301120 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=10 December 2020}}</ref> The draw for the fourth and fifth round were made on 11 January, conducted by [[Peter Crouch]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth and fifth round draw made |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/jan/11/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-and-fifth-round-draws-20211101 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> In the fourth round, Chelsea overcame [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] by a score of 3–1, with [[Tammy Abraham]] scoring all three goals for his side. In doing so, Abraham became the first Englishman to a score a hat-trick for Chelsea in the FA Cup since manager [[Frank Lampard]] in [[2006–07 FA Cup|2007]], and he became the first Chelsea youth team product to score ten or more goals in back-to-back seasons since [[Mike Fillery]] in [[1982–83 Football League|1982–83]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/abraham-matches-lampard-with-fa-cup-hat-trick-for-chelsea-vs/1kznpisap182s1eyvjen7okf4l|title=Abraham matches Lampard with FA Cup hat-trick for Chelsea vs Luton|website=Goal|date=24 January 2021|access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref> The match against Luton Town was Lampard's last in charge as he was sacked the following day.<ref name="ESPNTuchel" /> The draw for the quarter-finals was made, live on [[BT Sport]] by [[Karen Carney]] on 11 February.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/feb/11/emirates-fa-cup-quarter-final-draw-20210211 | title=The draw for the quarter-final of the Emirates FA Cup was made on Thursday evening | website=The FA |publisher=The Football Association |date=11 February 2021 | access-date=11 February 2021}}</ref> The draw for the semi-finals was made, live on [[BBC One]] by [[Dion Dublin]] on 21 March.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/mar/21/emirates-fa-cup-semi-final-draw-20210321 | title=See the line-up for this season's Emirates FA Cup semi-finals after Sunday's draw | website=The FA |publisher=The Football Association | date=21 March 2021 | access-date=21 March 2021}}</ref> Chelsea reached the [[2021 FA Cup Final]] after defeating [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] 1–0 in the semi-final with a goal from [[Hakim Ziyech]]. However, Chelsea would end up losing the final 1–0 to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] following a controversial goal from [[Youri Tielemans]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Phil|last=McNulty|title= Youri Tielemans produced one of the great FA Cup final goals to give Leicester City the trophy for the first time in their history with victory over Chelsea at Wembley|date=15 May 2021|website=BBC.com|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57055571|access-date=17 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57055571|title=Chelsea 0 v Leicester City 1|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=15 May 2021|access-date=15 May 2021}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2020–21 EFL Cup}}

The draw for both the second and third round were confirmed on September 6, live on [[Sky Sports]] by [[Phil Babb]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup: Round Two and Three draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2020/september/carabao-cup-round-two-draw-confirmed/ |access-date=6 September 2020 |publisher=[[English Football League]] |date=6 September 2020}}</ref> In the third round, Chelsea were drawn at home against [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]]. [[Tammy Abraham]] opened the scoring in the 19th minute, slotting past former Blues keeper [[Bradley Collins|Brad Collins]]. New signing [[Kai Havertz]] then latched on to [[Mason Mount]]'s pass after a clever Abraham dummy and slid left-footed effort into the bottom corner to open his Chelsea account.<ref name="BBCefl" /> [[Ross Barkley]] made it three after the break before Abraham's neat flick teed Havertz up for a simple finish inside the area. Abraham then found Havertz for his hat-trick goal in the 65th minute and [[Olivier Giroud]] finished the scoring to make it 6–0 with seven minutes to go.<ref name="BBCefl">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54190608|title=Kai Havertz's hat-trick in Chelsea's Carabao Cup thrashing of Barnsley will be the "first of many great nights" for him, says Blues boss Frank Lampard.|website=BBC|date=23 September 2020|access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref>

The fourth round draw was conducted on 17 September 2020 by [[Laura Woods (English presenter)|Laura Woods]] and [[Lee Hendrie]] live on [[Sky Sports]]; Chelsea were handed an away game against Tottenham Hotspur, led by former manager [[José Mourinho]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Carabao Cup: Round Four draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2020/september/carabao-cup-round-four-draw-confirmed/|publisher=English Football League|access-date=23 September 2020 |language=en-gb |date=17 September 2020}}</ref> Chelsea went in front against Spurs with new signing Timo Werner netting his first goal for the club in the 19th minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/match/tottenham-hotspur-v-chelsea/sagg9rj0febpb8zztm0shm38 |title=Tottenham 1-1 Chelsea (5-4 pens): Werner off the mark but Mount miss sends Spurs through |website=Goal |date=30 September 2020 |access-date=30 September 2020}}</ref> However, [[Erik Lamela]] would equalize for Tottenham with six minutes to go and the hosts would go on to win in the penalty shoot-out after a solitary miss from Chelsea midfielder [[Mason Mount]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-vs-chelsea/438838|title=Tottenham 1-1 Chelsea (5-4 pens): Spurs through to Carabao Cup quarter-finals on penalties after late equaliser|website=Sky Sports|date=29 September 2020|access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref>

===UEFA Champions League===
{{main|2020–21 UEFA Champions League}}
The group stage draw was held on 1 October 2020 with Chelsea being placed in Group E along with [[2020 UEFA Europa League Final|Europa League]] holders [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] and two competition debutants in [[FC Krasnodar|Krasnodar]] of [[Russian Premier League|Russia]] and [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Stade Rennes]] of [[Ligue 1|France]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0262-1081d9c1805c-fff671c9455e-1000--champions-league-group-stage-draw-made/|title=Champions League group stage draw made in Geneva|date=1 October 2020|access-date=1 October 2020|website=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> Chelsea progressed as group winners having won four matches and drawing the other two.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0263-10f48bbd46dc-ae3c418e73d2-1000--champions-league-group-stage-permutations-who-needs-what-to-rea/|title=Champions League group stage permutations: Who needs what to reach the round of 16?|website=UEFA|date=9 December 2020|access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref> This included a convincing 4–0 away win versus [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] with [[Olivier Giroud]] scoring all four. In the draw for the round of 16, Chelsea were pitted against Spanish side [[Atlético Madrid]], setting up the eighth and ninth matches between the clubs in just over a decade, following group stage clashes in [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League|2009–10]], a solitary matchup in the [[2012 UEFA Super Cup]], a semi-final tie in [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|2013–14]], and another group stage meeting in the Champions League in [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2020/12/14/champions-league-round-of-16-draw|title=Chelsea to Face Atletico Madrid in Champions League Round of 16|website=Chelsea FC|date=14 December 2020|access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref> Chelsea would go on to win the first leg 1–0 after a goal from Olivier Giroud. Chelsea moved on to the quarter-finals after a 2–0 second-leg win, with a goal in each half from [[Hakim Ziyech]] and [[Emerson Palmieri|Emerson]], and were drawn against [[FC Porto]]. It was the ninth meeting between the two clubs, the most recent being a 2–0 Chelsea victory in the group stage of the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/chelsea-vs-fc-porto-complete-head-to-head-record|title=Chelsea vs FC Porto: Complete head-to-head record|website=90 Min|date=19 March 2021|access-date=21 March 2021}}</ref> Chelsea defeated Porto 2–0 in the first match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/matches/match-day/2020/2197666?pageTab=news|title=FC Porto vs Chelsea - 7 April 2021 - Champions League|website=chelseafc.com|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=7 April 2021|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref> They advanced 2–1 on aggregate despite losing 1–0 in the second leg to Porto. By doing this, Chelsea reached the Semi-finals, a feat they had not accomplished since [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|2013–14]] campaign. Chelsea were drawn against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the Semi-finals. The first leg was played in the [[Alfredo Di Stéfano Stadium|Alfredo Di Stéfano]]. [[Christian Pulisic]] gave Chelsea the lead before [[Karim Benzema]] equalized for the home side, the match ended in a 1–1 draw. In the second leg at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], [[Timo Werner]] and [[Mason Mount]] gave Chelsea a 2–0 win (3–1 on aggregate). This meant that Chelsea would be in the [[2021 Champions League Final|final]], the first time Chelsea had reached the final since the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|2011–12]] campaign. In the final at the [[Estádio do Dragão]], Chelsea would emerge victorious against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] 1–0 with a goal from [[Kai Havertz]] sealing their first Champions League title since the 2011–12 campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57268064|title=Kai Havertz goal secures Champions League title for Chelsea|website=BBC Sport|date=29 May 2021|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref>

=====Final=====
{{Football box collapsible
|round = [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final|Final]]
|date = 29 May 2021
|time = 20:00 [[Western European Summer Time|WEST]] [[Time in Portugal|PTT]] ([[UTC+01:00|UTC+1]])
|team1 = [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] {{fbaicon|ENG}}
|score = 0–1
|report = https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2029498/
|team2 = {{fbaicon|ENG}} Chelsea
|goals1 = [[İlkay Gündoğan|Gündoğan]] {{yel|35}}<br>[[Gabriel Jesus]] {{yel|88}}
|goals2 = [[Kai Havertz|Havertz]] {{goal|42}}<br>[[Antonio Rüdiger|Rüdiger]] {{yel|57}}
|stadium = [[Estádio do Dragão]]
|location = [[Porto]], Portugal
|attendance = 14,110
|referee = [[Antonio Mateu Lahoz]] ([[Royal Spanish Football Federation|Spain]])
|result = W
|note = The final was originally scheduled to be played in [[Atatürk Olympic Stadium]] in [[Istanbul]]. However, on 12 May, UEFA announced it had been moved to Portugal since the high COVID-19 infection rates in Turkey had led the UK government to place travel to Turkey on its red-list, meaning fans would have had to quarantine for ten days in a hotel at their expense on their return. Portugal at the same time was on the green-list which meant no travel restrictions at either end for those attending the final.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0269-1243f864391e-53c7874f0ae0-1000/|title=UEFA Champions League final to move to Portugal to allow 6,000 fans of each team to attend|website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=13 May 2021|access-date=13 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57071221|title=Champions League final moved to Porto and 12,000 Chelsea and Manchester City fans can attend|website=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2021|access-date=13 May 2021}}</ref>
}}
